purpose: Selection register for mutually exclusive coordination and locking providers.
Records why one candidate is chosen over the other; it does not deploy either.

when: Coordination stays on one host or on hosts that already share a synchronized folder.
No external service may be introduced; the coordination layer must work offline.
The claim only has to be visible to agents and humans reading the project folder.
A lock has to be readable and removable without any tooling, including by hand.
strengths: File-based: LOCK*.txt in the project folder is the sole authority; cache, SQLite and web UI are derived views.
Zero infrastructure: network boundary 'none', data boundary 'user-local', runs on windows, macos and linux.
Agent-neutral permission model LOCK.permissions.json with precedence deny > ask > allow.
Operationally proven and public: status active, visibility public, surfaces library, cli and workflow.
tradeoffs: No transactional guarantee: two agents starting at the same moment can both observe an empty folder.
Coordination stops at the folder boundary; hosts without the shared folder cannot participate.
No memory of outcomes; a lock records a claim, not how the attempt ended.
Stale locks need the 24h expiry net or prune_stale_locks.py; user locks never expire by design.
evidence: registry:modules#lock-master (boundaries.network none, boundaries.data user-local, kind protocol, status active, visibility public, provides control.locks and control.permissions)
_scripts/LOCK-SYSTEM.md (lock types, precedence deny > ask > allow, expiry, authority of the LOCK*.txt files)

when: Agents that do not know each other must be coordinated across vendors, machines and sessions.
Double work has to be prevented by a transaction, not by an observation of the file system.
The question 'has this been attempted before, and how did it end?' has to be answerable.
An external managed database is acceptable as the system of record.
strengths: CockroachDB is the system of record: serializable leases instead of best-effort file claims.
Outcome memory through a distributed vector index, failures included.
Explicitly vendor-neutral; the gap no vendor has an interest in closing.
Narrow agent-facing write path through roshambo-mcp with enforced invariants instead of free SQL.
tradeoffs: Requires external infrastructure: CockroachDB Cloud plus Bedrock, Lambda and S3, all declared status planned.
Not local-first: stack policy local_first is false, network policy declared, platforms limited to windows and linux.
Maturity: stack status development, visibility public-candidate, created for a competition deadline.
Data boundary rises to sensitive, so an anonymizer has to run before anything becomes swarm-visible.
evidence: .STACKS/NEW-STACK_ROSHAMBO.md (purpose, system of record, positioning, size class mix-stack, deliberate gaps)
.STACKS/roshambo-stack/stack.v2.json (policies.local_first false, policies.network declared, external_components status planned, visibility public-candidate)

choice_groups.relationship_note: The two candidates are an alternative pair and a dependency at the same time: roshambo adopts lock-master's lease semantics (claim, expiry, rights with precedence deny > ask > allow) and only moves the storage from LOCK*.txt to a database table. Choosing roshambo therefore does not discard lock-master's model, it relocates it. Source: .STACKS/NEW-STACK_ROSHAMBO.md, packing list row 'lock-master | Lease-Semantik'.
choice_groups.selection_notes: Decide by reach, not by feature count: within one host or one synchronized folder lock-master is sufficient and cheaper by an order of magnitude; across vendors, machines and sessions a file cannot carry the guarantee and roshambo becomes the honest answer.
